title: Ripple round motif
subtitle: A flat circular motif with a concentric wave pattern built from increases and decreases
excerpt: The ripple round alternates dc increase peaks and dc2tog decrease valleys on every other round, producing a flat circle with a concentric wave line across the surface. Four rounds in DK cotton make a 12 cm circle with one wave ring visible; six rounds make two visible rings.
sourceNotes: Ripple and chevron construction in circular form appears in Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), wave motif chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A ripple round crochet motif in two shades of ocean blue DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Concentric wave rings across the flat circle, 12 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished ripple round measures 12 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Ripple round motif
chartDefinition.caption: Even rounds: standard flat-circle increases (2dc in every other st). Odd rounds: ripple round — 2dc in peak positions, dc2tog at valley positions.

glossaryTerms.definition: A 2dc increase worked at the peak position of a ripple round, creating a raised bump at the outer edge of each wave. Alternates with dc2tog valleys to maintain the stitch count and keep the circle flat.

content.text: The ripple round motif alternates a standard flat-circle increase round with a

round, where increases at peak positions and dc2tog at valleys create the wave texture while keeping the circle flat. The stitch count stays consistent because each ripple round adds as many stitches as it removes.

Work the flat rounds in one colour and the ripple rounds in a second colour to make the wave rings visible. Two ripple rounds nested inside a 12 cm circle require a careful stitch count — mark the peak and valley positions after round 2 with stitch markers.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g colour A and 4 g colour B in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Stitch markers.

content.text: Magic ring. 8 dc into ring. Sl st to join. (8 dc.)
2 dc into every dc around. Sl st to join. (16 dc.)
Mark 8 peak positions (every other dc from round 2). At each peak: 2 dc. Between peaks: 1 dc, dc2tog, 1 dc. Sl st to join. (Stitch count stays at 16.)
2 dc into every other dc, 1 dc into remaining dc. Sl st to join. (24 dc.) Continue for further ripple rounds as desired.
